messages:
maria: quick follow-up from today's all-hands re: pricing/credits / proration and burst fairness. two customer asks: 1) if a tenant upgrades mid-cycle, how is proration handled? 2) how do we enforce fair-share during noisy bursts on shared hosted pools?
phil: short answers: 1) we prorate remaining days and apply a credit/charge adjustment on the next invoice. 2) we have a per-tenant fair-share window + emergency override for pilot customers.
lucy: proration detail: when plan changes, billing creates a ledger adjustment: prorated_credit = old_plan_daily_rate * days_remaining - new_plan_daily_rate * days_remaining (sign flips as needed). we record adjustment_id and show on invoice.
arun: infra fairness: hosted pools enforce a sliding-window token cap per org (e.g., 60s window). if an org exceeds its share we throttle to target qps for the window. this prevents one noisy tenant from saturating a GPU.
emma: customers asked about strictness: can they opt-out to preference for throughput over fairness? answer: orgs on Dedicated or reserved capacity can set their own share; hosted customers use default fair-share and can request higher quotas via support.
billing-bot: note: ledger entries look like: {"id":"adj_123","type":"proration","amount_cents":-4500,"reason":"upgrade"}. adjustments appear on next invoice and in console ledger.
ops-bot: emergency override: SRE can issue an `override_token` to temporarily raise per-tenant caps for incidents. issuance creates an immutable audit event and a TTL (default 10m). usage of override is gated to on-call + product manager approval.
maria: leadership Q: can we expose a self-serve emergency uplift in the console for org admins (with billing consequences shown)? some customers asked for faster mitigations without going through SRE.
phil: product stance: acceptable for paid-tier orgs under guardrails. UX should require org admin confirmation, show estimated cost delta, and create an automatic rollback/timebox. legal wants an acknowledgement for SLA/quality drift.
lucy: billing implication: uplift creates a temporary quota bucket charged at an overage rate. we should show an estimated cost preview before applying. ledger will record uplift events separately.
arun: implementation notes: uplift flow = create ephemeral token + allocate extra capacity from pool + backfill accounting. must lock allocation to avoid race with autoscaler. also emit trace id so customers can correlate.
emma: another ask: how do credits expire when using proration credits? if you get prorated credit from downgrade, does it expire?
billing-bot: policy: prorated credits applied to the billing ledger and expire per org default (90 days) unless promotional terms say otherwise. show expiry in console.
maria: action items: 1) doc proration flow + examples (owner @lucy). 2) spec for fair-share windows + uplift UI (owner @arun + @phil). 3) billing UX for uplift cost-preview and expiry display (owner @emma). 4) SRE runbook for override_token issuance (owner @ops-bot).
phil: ping owners to post short proposals in the all-hands PR by EOD Friday. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
